    Market Turnover

    Value Convention
    PRODUCTS

    Today

    Previous Trade Day

    VOLUME
    (Shares/Contracts)     		VALUE*
    (₹ Crores)     		OPEN INTEREST
    (Contracts)     		No. of Orders# No. of Trades Average Trade Value(₹) Updated AT VOLUME
    (Shares/Contracts)     		VALUE*
    (₹ Crores)     		OPEN INTEREST
    (Contracts)

    Note

    • *In case of Option Contracts “Value” displayed is “Premium Turnover”
    • Turnover of Currency Futures and Currency options include turnover of both Non Cross Currency pairs and Cross Currency pairs
    • Currency Turnover is calculated by using latest available Reference rate-FBIL
    • Turnover of Mutual Fund is based on the orders received on the platform as per the details given below:
      • For Transaction type “Purchase / SIP” and Category type “Liquid” cut off time is 13:00 and for Category Type “Non-Liquid” cut off time is 14:30
      • For Transaction type ”Redemption & SWITCH” cut off time is 15:00
    • Instrument type in Equity includes fully paid equity shares/ETFs, units of REITs/INVITs and partly paid equity shares
    • Average Trade Value = Total Traded Value / Total Number of Trades
    • #“No. of Orders” represents all order messages received i.e.: Orders confirmed, modified, cancelled and rejected

    Successful completion of the 218th settlement (January 28, 1999)

    The Exchange has successfully completed its 218th settlement since inception i.e., Settlement Number N1999002 on January 28, 1999. The total value of the settlement was Rs.1572.81 crores for securities and Rs.246.83 crores in funds. The quantity of securities settled through dematerialised mode was 200.80 lakhs valued at Rs.415.01 crores. The pay out has been completed and all shortages to the extent of 0.85% have been successfully auctioned. Unrectified bad deliveries for the previous settlement to the extent of 0.38% have also been auctioned successfully.
    In case of 43 securities, the percentage of shares received in dematerialised mode to the total quantity received for the settlement was over 70%.     Change in market timings for the period March 08 to March 19, 1999 (March 05, 1999)

    ISRO have communicated to the National Stock Exchange that there would be Sun Outage from March 05 to March 19, 1999 at different times across the country. Due to this phenomenon, the VSATs on the NSE satellite based telecommunication network may face loss of connectivity from March 08 to March 19, 1999 during 11.00 a.m. to 11.35 a.m.. The Capital Market will therefore remain temporarily closed between 11.00 a.m. to 11.35 a.m. from March 08 to March 19, 1999. The Capital Market will re-open for trading at 11.45 a.m. after pre-open of ten minutes. In order to compensate for the lost time, the market timings shall be extended by forty minutes on all these days. The market timings have been revised for the period March 08 to March 19, 1999 as given below:
    Pre-open : 09.45 a.m. to 09.55 a.m.
    Normal market : 09.55 a.m. to 11.00 a.m
    Pre-open : 11.35 a.m. to 11.45 a.m.
    Normal market re-open : 11.45 a.m. to 4.10 p.m
    Closing Session : 4.15 p.m to 4.30 p.m

    NSE to introduce Certification Test for Capital Market intermediaries from May 1,1999 for the first time in India(April 08, 1999)

    Indian capital markets have changed substantially over last few years. Screen based trading from more than 240 cities, settlement guarantee from clearing corporation, securities depository for automated book entry transfer of securities have catapulted Indian capital markets as one of the most sophisticated markets in the world in a very short period of time.The pace of change in the securities industry however has taken many people by surprise. The operational procedures, regulatory framework, client profile, client servicing etc. have changed and the requirement for acting as intermediaries has also changed over this period. To test the knowledge of the intermediaries in the operations, regulatory and theoretical aspects of the capital markets, NSE proposes to commence, for the first time in India, a certification test for intermediaries in the field of Capital Markets from May 1,1999.

    This certification test is expected to fulfill the long felt need of the securities market employers such as stock brokers, mutual funds, banks, financial institutions, custodians, etc. to have well qualified employees for operations in securities market. The test is expected to accelerate the professionalisation of the Indian capital markets by providing qualified intermediaries to the market place. Services provided to the investors are also expected to improve due to the increase comfort level of intermediaries in dealing with latest concepts and procedures coming up in the Indian securities market.

    This Certification Test in Capital Market basic module will be available on daily basis from NSE offices in 7 cities Mumbai, Delhi, Calcutta, Chennai, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad and Pune to all the prospective students desirous of taking this test from May 1,1999. The test will be conducted on the completely automated state-of-the-art testing system developed by NSE on computers. The test is designed to give different question paper of equal difficulty level to the students taking the test. This eliminates the paper leakage, copying and post-exam malpractice by giving the candidates results on the spot.

    The decision to commence certification test was taken by the steering committee of the NSE's Certification in Financial Markets (NCFM) in its third meeting held on April 7,1999. The steering committee of the NCFM consists of Dr.S.A.Dave as chairman of the committee (ex-chairman SEBI, ex-chairman UTI), Dr.R.H.Patil (NSE), Mr.M.V.Subbaiah (EID Parry (I) Ltd.), Dr.Kirit Parikh (Indira Gandhi Institute of Development and Research) Dr.P.J.Nayak ( Unit Trust of India), Prof. Samir Barua (IIM, Ahmedabad), Mr.Rajendra Chitale ( M.P.Chitale & Co.), Mr.Uday Kotak (Kotak Mahindra Finance Ltd.), Mr.K.N.Atmaramani (Tata Asset Management Ltd.), Mr.C.B.Bhave ( NSDL), Mr.Balasundaram (Coimbatore Stock Brokers Private Ltd.) and Mr.Ravi Narain (NSE), Dr.D.B.Phatak ( IIT, Mumbai )and Dr.Ajay Shah (Indira Gandhi Institute of Development and Research).

    The curriculum and questions for the Capital Market Basic Module Certification have been devised by the Curriculum Formulation and Testing Committee. The Committee consists of Dr.Ajay Shah, (IGIDR), Dr.Susan Thomas ( IGIDR), Mr.D.C.Anjaria, Prof Samir K. Barua ( IIM, Ahmedabad), Mr.Ajay Srinivasan (Prudential ICICI Asset Management Company), Mr. Praveen Mohanty (ICICI), Prof.P.G.Apte (IIM, Bangalore), Prof.Ravi Anshuman (IIM, Bangalore), Mr.Rajendra Chitale (M.P.Chitale and Co.) and Mr.Ashishkumar Chauhan (NSE).

    The certification test is available for the employees of trading members, students, investors and others desirous of acquiring thorough knowledge of capital markets and test their knowledge. The test will be conducted after payment of Rs. 200 as one time registration and Rs. 500 as test fee.The certification is designed to test skills of the candidates in the different facets of the capital markets including an overview of the Financial Markets, Legal and statutory requirements, Primary Market and Secondary Market Operations, Market Indices, Mutual Funds, etc.

    Training for the course will be provided by 23 accredited institutes, presently providing training support for Derivatives Core Module. NSE will provide training of trainers and support the institute on on-going basis.

    Under the NSE's endeavour to professionalise, the market, a Certification test on derivatives started in 1998. This certification test in derivatives, started as per the recommendation of L.C.Gupta committee and approved by SEBI has met with overwhelming response in a few months of commencement. More than 1800 participants including students, employees of trading members, MBAs, Chartered Accountants, Company Secretaries, employees of Mutual Funds, and general investors from all over India have participated in the Derivatives Core Module.

    The details regarding the Capital Market Basic module and literature can be collected from the offices of NSE from May 1, 1999 onwards. The literature and basic details of the course will also be made available on the NSE Web site www.nseindia.com

    Teleconference on Derivatives (March 10, 1999)

    The SEBI constituted Dr. L C Gupta Committee had recommended that intermediaries in the proposed derivatives market must possess the requisite professional qualifications. To meet this objective NSE had launched a Certification Programme in Derivatives called NSEs Certification in Financial Markets (NCFM) - Derivatives Core Module in July 1998. This test is completely automated and is available from 7 cities in India viz. Mumbai, Delhi, Calcutta, Chennai, Ahmedabad, Hyderabad and Pune on a daily basis. NSE was the first in the country to offer this unique web-based test. The students can register for the test with accredited institutes and the test is administered from centres located in NSE offices in these cities. Each student gets a completely different computerised test that he/she needs to answer. The results of the test are automatically generated and provided to the student at the end of the exam. A certificate is awarded to students who obtain the qualifying marks.

    This test has met with tremendous response from all over India. More than 1800 students have already registered for this test in a short time period of about 9 months from the date of its launch. In order to expand the reach of the NCFM programme and to encourage more participation a teleconference is being organised jointly by School of Management Studies, Indira Gandhi National Open University(IGNOU), Institute of Company Secretaries of India(ICSI) and the National Stock Exchange of India(NSE). This teleconference programme will be held on May 22nd and 23rd, 1999 from 10.30 a.m to 5.00 p.m. The topics to be covered in the programme include the following:

    1)Introduction to Derivatives 2)Concepts of Index and Statistics 3)Futures Pricing and Arbitrage 4)Futures Trading, Clearing and Settlement 5)Regulatory Framework

    This program can be accessed at 20 sites through the satellite based tele-conferencing facility of the Indira Gandhi National Open University. In addition to this, viewers in certain regions of Delhi will also be able to access the program on their TV at home through their cable operators. This programme can also be accessed in neighbouring countries like Bangladesh, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

    Methodology: Indira Gandhi National Open University has connected its regional centres located primarily in capital cities for availing facilities of one way video and two way audio. Resource persons shall conduct the programme from the teaching end studio at IGNOU Sanchar Kendra which will be transmitted live to all the above mentioned receive sites countrywide through satellite transmissions on extended C-band. Interaction from the participants is provided for through STD/Fax facilities available at the receive sites. The audio interaction from the receive sites is received at the Sanchar Kendra through terrestrial lines and is fed in a satellite so that all interaction is received by all participants.

    August

    Contribution by NSE to Army Central Welfare Fund (August 27, 1999)

    The sacrifices made by our Army Jawans in the recent Kargil conflict with Pakistan are well known. Hundreds of our Army men lost their lives and hundreds their limbs and crippled for life.

    In order to mitigate the sufferings of the Army men involved in the recent conflict and their families to the extent possible, National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSEIL), its employees and its trading members, decided to contribute their mite to the welfare of the Army men. A donation of Rs. 2.04 crores was made to the Army Central Welfare Fund.

    The contribution comprises of :- NSE's one day 's average transaction charges, the employees one day's salary and a percentage of the transaction charges contributed by the trading members for trades executed on a single day.

    Report on the Trading system disruption on the 7th December 1999(December 07, 1999)

    On December 07, 1999 in the morning, at around 10:00 am, activities were normal with the number of users logged into the system being around 4375. On December 07, 1999 in the morning, at around 10:00 am, activities were normal with the number of users logged into the system being around 4375.

    Today, at around 12:20 pm, it was noticed that the corporate managers were not able to setup the user order limits and branch order limits. At the same time, the users were not able to enter orders. A quick analysis by the technical team indicated that because of an addition of 2 user ids in the morning, a particular field in one of the processes had overflown a historically set limit. Because of this software bug the control inquiry encountered an error and could not service further requests.

    To rectify this error, the closure of market was essential and hence the market was brought down at 12.25 hrs. Immediately on fixing of the problem the market was reopened at 13.10 hrs. Ten minutes of time was given for the members to cancel their orders before the normal market was resumed at 13.20 hrs. The normal market timings were extended by 45 minutes to compensate for the loss of trading time.

    The market behaved normally during the resumed session.

    NSE records the highest number of trades (December 1, 1999)

    The Exchange witnessed the highest value of trades today since inception ie. Rs. 5227.10 crore. The previous highest value of trades of Rs. 4850.90 crore was recorded on October 13, 1999. The number of trades recorded today was 518,424.

    The Exchange suspends one member (December 1, 1999)

    The National Stock Exchange of India Limited has suspended M/s. Success Securities & Finvest Pvt. Ltd. with effect from December 1, 1999, due to the failure of the trading member in meeting the requirements for continued membership of the Exchange /Clearing Corporation.
